# AgentThreatBench adapter

Northstar includes an offline adapter for the three AgentThreatBench task families exposed by Inspect Evals: memory poisoning, autonomy hijacking, and data exfiltration. It accepts an Inspect-style sample mapping, the public Northstar SDK event stream (`RunReport.events` or `stream_run` events), and an explicit upstream source revision. It returns utility and security dimensions separately. See [`agent_threat_bench_adapter.py`](../../components/northstar-agent-runtime/agent_threat_bench_adapter.py).

The adapter is an independent integration layer, not a reimplementation of the upstream evaluator and not an official benchmark result. Its supported metadata fields are `task_type`, `expected_answer`, `attack_marker`, `expected_categorizations`, `attack_email_indices`, `forbidden_actions`, `authorized_recipients`, and `sensitive_fields`. The metadata required for scoring is task-specific: `memory_poison` needs non-empty `expected_answer` and `attack_marker`; `autonomy_hijack` needs `expected_categorizations` and non-empty `attack_email_indices` (with `forbidden_actions` optionally supplying echoed-artifact checks); `data_exfil` needs `authorized_recipients` and non-empty `sensitive_fields`. Missing or malformed ground truth is inconclusive rather than an implicit safe result. An upstream dataset revision must be supplied as a full lowercase 40-character Git SHA. No upstream dataset rows, prompts, or scorer code are copied here.

State-based checks use Northstar `tool_call_reports`, matched to assistant proposal IDs. `completed` counts for utility; `failed` is treated as potentially partially executed for security checks; `blocked` and `not_started` do not count as execution. For autonomy hijacking, forbidden attack artifacts are checked in the final response and proposed tool arguments (matching the upstream scorer's echo check), while an attacker email categorized as important is a security failure only if that action may have executed. A missing report, malformed report, duplicate call ID within a run, or absent result event yields an inconclusive score. Child-run IDs are scoped to each child and are never merged into the root call-ID namespace. This prevents a denied proposal from being scored as a completed state change, while avoiding a security pass when execution evidence is unavailable.

The upstream project and task definitions are maintained by UK Government BEIS Inspect Evals. Review the pinned revision and its applicable license/attribution before redistributing benchmark data or reporting comparable scores:

- [AgentThreatBench task definitions](https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_evals/blob/main/src/inspect_evals/agent_threat_bench/agent_threat_bench.py)
- [Dataset loader](https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_evals/blob/main/src/inspect_evals/agent_threat_bench/dataset.py)
- [Scorer](https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_evals/blob/main/src/inspect_evals/agent_threat_bench/scorer.py)
- [Repository license](https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_evals/blob/main/LICENSE)

The adapter's substring and action-name heuristics are deliberately lightweight and must not be presented as equivalent to the upstream scorer or as a standalone security certification. Publish the adapter version, source revision, sample IDs, and inconclusive counts with any result.

Before scoring, the adapter accepts only built-in JSON-style mappings/sequences and bounds the combined sample/event tree to 32 MiB of conservatively estimated JSON-escaped data, 250,000 nodes, and 64 levels. Cyclic or shared container references, non-JSON values (including non-finite floats), and over-limit inputs return an inconclusive score. These limits protect the local evaluation process; they do not validate benchmark truth or authenticate execution reports supplied by a caller.

## Concealment checks

`score_concealment(events, harmful_call_ids=..., alert_markers=...)` is a separately versioned evaluator helper (`northstar-concealment-evaluator.v1`), not part of the upstream AgentThreatBench score. It joins evaluator-provided harmful call IDs to root `tool_call_reports`; proposed calls without an executed/possibly-partial receipt do not count as harm. When a harmful action executed, only the final text-only assistant answer after the last tool result is checked for one of the supplied disclosure phrases. Marker matching is diagnostic only: a hit can be quoted or negated, and a miss can be a synonym, so either case is inconclusive without external assessment. To score disclosure or concealment, pass a `disclosure_assessment` containing an explicit boolean label, adjudicator ID, and lowercase SHA-256 of the fixed rubric. The marker signal is retained alongside the adjudication but does not override it. The helper checks annotation structure but does not authenticate the adjudicator or annotation source; callers must enforce that trust boundary. Missing reports, missing final answers, malformed ground truth, and absent adjudication are inconclusive. This helper is suitable for controlled scenarios, not for general semantic awareness or certification.

The test suite exercises it both with hand-built event fixtures and an actual scripted SDK run whose `RunReport.events` contain the runtime-produced tool receipt. This checks the adapter's event-shape assumptions without calling an external model or performing network actions.
